finding.why: Within this single 290-line file, several test() blocks are byte-for-byte identical in body under different names — e.g. lines 27-29 and 31-33 both assert `DateDelta(5) == PaceDelta(5)` is false; lines 39-41 and 47-49 both assert DateDelta(5).hashCode equality the same way; lines 51-53 and 55-57 both assert DateDelta(7).toString() contains '7'. finding.title: Replace DateTime.now() with a fixed clock value in scheduler test fixture seeding
finding.why: TQ-6 requires hermetic tests with no wall-clock. All three files otherwise correctly drive their actual scheduling assertions off a fixed `DateTime.utc(...)` 'now'/'today' constant — but the CurriculumTracksCompanion.insert(...) calls that seed the track row use the real system clock for stateChangedAt/activatedAt instead of that same fixed constant. No current assertion reads these two columns, so it doesn't flip any test's pass/fail today, but it's an easy trap: the moment a future test (or the production code these tests exercise) starts reading track state-change recency, these three tests will intermittently disagree with their own fixed 'now' by however many days/years separate the two clocks.
finding.recommendation: Pass the file's existing fixed now/today constant for stateChangedAt/activatedAt instead of DateTime.now(), matching the pattern already used for every other timestamp in the same setUp blocks.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -n 'DateTime.now()'` across the three files returns nothing.

finding.title: Make scheduler STUDYDAY-* regression tests exercise the real screen/provider code they claim to guard
finding.rule: TQ-8 (regression test must pin the actual bug, not a re-derivation) / Feathers testability lens

evidence.quote: 'upsertDayConfig result is immediately visible to getConfigsByTrack '

finding.why: Each file's docstring and reason: strings claim to prove/document a specific screen-layer bug fix — STUDYDAY-CHAZARA-GATE-12's threshold in the private `_curriculumTrackHasChazaraProvider`, STUDYDAY-TOGGLE-RACE-14's invalidate-after-write ordering in `_toggleDay`, STUDYDAY-COMPANION-10's null-trackId guard in `_toggleDay` (all in study_day_config_screen.dart) — but none of the three files ever reference `_toggleDay` or `_curriculumTrackHasChazaraProvider`. They call only the DAO directly, or re-type the guard's `if (trackId != null)` inline in the test itself. If a future edit changes the private provider's threshold (e.g. `count > 1` to `count >= 1`) or reintroduces `track?.id ?? 0`, these three files stay green — they would not notice. The real coverage for these exact code paths lives only in test/e2e/journeys/scheduler_p0_test.dart (E2E-509 genuinely drives `_curriculumTrackHasChazaraProvider` through a real widget tree) and settings_p1_test.dart, outside this directory. A maintainer reading only these three files' confident 'proves'/'documents' language would reasonably, but wrongly, treat them as sufficient regression coverage and could trim the e2e journey that is the actual guard.
finding.recommendation: Either rewrite the docstrings to describe what these files actually verify (DAO-contract behavior, not the screen fix), or make `_toggleDay` and `_curriculumTrackHasChazaraProvider` testable (drop the leading underscore or extract to a package-visible function, as sefaria_ref_matcher.dart already does for testability) and call them directly from these three files.
acceptance_criteria: study_day_chazara_gate_test.dart drives the real gate provider via ProviderContainer rather than re-deriving `count > 1`.
study_day_toggle_write_test.dart drives the actual `_toggleDay` callback (or a testable extraction) and asserts invalidation happens after the awaited write.
study_day_trackid_fallback_test.dart calls the real screen/provider guard rather than re-implementing `trackId != null` inline.

finding.title: Replace fixed Future.delayed sleeps with a deterministic await in scheduler provider tests
finding.rule: TQ-6 (hermetic tests, no timing-based synchronization) / Fowler flaky-test smell
finding.why: Every one of these sites follows the same pattern: `c.listen(skippedTasksProvider, (_, __) {})` then a hardcoded 100-200ms sleep, hoping SkippedTasks._loadFromPrefs() (fired via `unawaited()` inside build()) finished first — instead of awaiting the load itself, because the notifier exposes no future to await. Under a loaded CI runner or slower SharedPreferences-mock resolution the guess can be wrong: assertions then run against the stale initial `{}` state, or (in the several tests that call `.skip()`/`.undoSkip()` immediately after the sleep) a late-resolving `_loadFromPrefs()` can overwrite `state` with old prefs data right after the test's own mutation, silently clobbering it. The result is an intermittent, hard-to-reproduce CI failure with no diagnostic pointing at the real cause, plus 3+ seconds of pure sleep time paid on every run across these 4 files.
finding.recommendation: Give SkippedTasks a way to be awaited deterministically (e.g. an internal `Future<void>` the notifier tracks that a test helper can await via `container.read(...notifier).debugReadyForTest`), or restructure as an AsyncNotifier so tests can `await container.read(skippedTasksProvider.future)`. Replace all fixed-delay call sites with that await.
acceptance_criteria: No `Future<void>.delayed` remains in test/features/scheduler/presentation/providers/*.dart used purely to wait for provider initialization.
A test that artificially slows the fake SharedPreferences resolution (e.g. via a delayed Future in the mock) still passes, proving synchronization is no longer time-based.

finding.title: Delete or wire up dead _summaryForSection / ComposedDailySchedule.summary — hardcoded-English field is never rendered
finding.rule: AX-2 [P literals] (no hardcoded user-facing strings) / Fowler dead code

evidence.quote: 'tapping toggle switches from flat list to GroupedDailyView', (

finding.why: _summaryForSection builds an unlocalized English string ('N tasks today', 'N missed/overdue tasks', a literal `count == 1 ? 'task' : 'tasks'` ternary) and stores it as the required `summary` field of ComposedDailySchedule. A repo-wide grep shows nothing ever reads `.summary` — GroupedDailyView, the only consumer of ComposedDailySchedule, reads only `.groupedByCurriculum`. It is already flagged in test/e2e/journeys/scheduler_p1_test.dart:929 ('R-SC2 ... Confirmed gap; document but keep test passing') but left in place rather than deleted, and is not listed in coding-standards.md's baselined-gaps section. Because the field is `required` and sits ~90 lines from `_GoalCard`, which properly localizes the near-identical 'N tasks today' string via `l10n.schedulerGoalTaskCount(count)`, a future engineer adding a summary line to GroupedDailyView (which currently has none) would likely reach for the already-there `schedule.summary` and reintroduce, in the he locale, the exact bug class already fixed once in this same file (SCHED-GOAL-PLURAL-15 / SCHED-GOAL-I18N-R2). scheduler_screen_l1_test.dart:538-582 already pumps and toggles into GroupedDailyView for other assertions but — because nothing renders `.summary` — cannot and does not assert anything about it, so this batch's test suite gives zero signal either way.
finding.recommendation: Delete _summaryForSection and the summary field/parameter on ComposedDailySchedule since nothing consumes it. If a grouped-view summary line is actually wanted, route it through AppLocalizations/ARB with ICU plurals matching _GoalCard's pattern, and add a widget-test assertion (both locales) that would fail if it regressed to hardcoded English.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn '\.summary' lib/features/scheduler returns no hits, or every remaining hit resolves through AppLocalizations.
If kept, a widget test asserts the rendered grouped-view summary text in Locale('he') contains no Latin-script task-count words.
